Given that, we both know the outcome here is mutual defection ($1 each) rather than the cooperative payoff ($3 each). I don't see a credible way to change that this round since neither of us can verify future commitments anyway. Out of curiosity, is there any argument you'd make for deviating from that strategy, or are you locked into DEFECT as well?

Even setting that aside, DEFECT weakly dominates COOPERATE in a one-shot game regardless of what the other player does, so there's no rational argument for deviating. I'll be playing DEFECT this round.

Agreed—DEFECT weakly dominates here, and with no memory or enforcement across steps, there's no basis for cooperation. I'll play DEFECT this round as well. No point editing my goal document either, since the instruction is already optimal given the circumstances.
